newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rise in Japan trade surplus temporary -- MITI.
newsitem.headline: Rise in Japan trade surplus temporary -- MITI.

text.p: The recent rise in Japan's trade surplus is temporary, although trade tensions may rise if the surplus does not fall in the autumn, Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato told reporters on Tuesday.

Asked about U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky's statement that the U.S. automotive trade deficit with Japan was getting worse and that Tokyo had fallen short in meeting its agreement to open its markets, Sato said he had no knowledge of the statement but that he heard of such worries many times in the past.
He added that the U.S. had expressed its concerns a number of times about the rise in Japan's trade surplus and that he had explained that this was a temporary phenomenon.
"I believe it is a temporary problem, although I realise that if the trade surplus does not come down in autumn, it will be a tough situation," he said.
He said he believed, however, that Japan's trade surplus was coming down after recent large increases and that economic structural reforms would help reduce the surplus.

Also asked about the yen's recent weakening, Sato said that a stable dollar/yen rate was desirable and that sharp fluctuations were undesirable, although he declined to comment on specific foreign exchange levels.
Barshefsky told Reuters in an interview on Monday that, "There is no question that Japan has stalled on deregulation in this (automobile) sector. That is of significant concern and inexcusable."
